A LEAD, NOT A LOCATION, recorded 22 September 2026. The title says ODD COLLATZ TREE, and the Collatz page of www.mikematics.de carries a section Directed Collatz graphs that is about exactly that and is published nowhere else. Saved verbatim at literature/sources/winkler-mikematics-collatz-page-2026-09-22.txt. Its content: a conjecture that the leaves of the first branches with the same number of columns form GROWTH BOUNDARIES closely related to the main-branch number 1, 5, 21, 85, ... = (4^n - 1)/3 in the same column; that every odd number up to a_n is reached in the forwardings of the first branches; that this ordering principle is FULLY VALID UP TO COLUMN S_8 with a_8 = 87381 and then fails; and an explicit first-outlier list for S_9 through S_14, beginning 349525: 300223, 263271, 316283, 210855 and ending 357913941: 336607519, 326201919, 299206683, 244651439, 217467945, 163100959. A principle that holds up to a column and then breaks is a THRESHOLD, and the tree is the odd Collatz tree, so this page is a plausible public trace of the manuscript's subject. IT IS ONLY THAT. The reference [10] description speaks of Beatty first passage at slope log2 3 on the opposite side of the boundary, and nothing on the page mentions Beatty, log2 3 or a one-sided bound. Do not cite the page as the manuscript and do not infer the manuscript's statements from it. What it is good for is a concrete question to put to the author alongside the request for the text. 

NOT ON HIS OWN WEBSITE EITHER, checked 22 September 2026. www.mikematics.de is open to plain curl (HTTP 200, no gate) and every page of it was enumerated: home, collatz-problem, publications, arxiv-preprints, oeis-contributions, diophantine-equations, prime-numbers, matheplanet-articles, wiki-contributions, links. The front page lists fifteen items under Latest research and the Collatz page lists his five Collatz articles; the site is exhaustive down to German expository pieces and a falling-coin physics note. CONNECTION THRESHOLDS APPEARS NOWHERE ON IT -- no title match for connection or threshold in any page of the site. His arXiv author page https://arxiv.org/a/winkler_m_2.html does not have it, nor does Semantic Scholar author 93805838, nor ORCID 0000-0003-4035-7242. Together with the routes already exhausted on 21 September, the conclusion is that it is unpublished, withdrawn, or absorbed into another title, and that citing reference [10] of the August 2026 revision is currently citing something the public cannot read. THE ONLY REMAINING ROUTE IS THE AUTHOR: mike.winkler@ruhr-uni-bochum.de. Stop spending probes on it.
